URL: (compiled) Monday 12 October 2026 MORNING ticker basis
Primary: CNBC quote endpoint, read 07:55 and 07:58 BST. Cross-check: Trading Economics (UK 10Y, Brent, US 10Y, GB100).

*** PUBLISHED BEFORE THE LONDON OPEN — TWO BASES, DECLARED ***
This edition is written between 07:55 and 08:25, so it goes out at or just after the open and inside the
known FTSE feed-lag window. Trading Economics is NOT a usable second provider for the FTSE pre-open: it
returns the identical stale value (GB100 10,552.05, dated Oct/09). So:

1. SHUT OR LAGGED, carrying Friday's close with Friday's session move:
   FTSE 10,552.05 +1.06 | SP 7,811.54 +0.59 | VIX 14.84 -3.70 | UST 5.24 +0.01
   The FTSE and S&P figures are the same ones Sunday evening published, for the same reason.
   CNBC reports the VIX change as UNCH because its prev field equals its last; -3.70 is published instead
   so that every lagged instrument on this ticker is measured on the same basis — Friday's close against
   Thursday's. Mixing a "no change since it last traded" figure in with four "Friday's session move"
   figures would be the only genuinely misleading option.
2. LIVE this morning:
   Brent 104.60 -0.11 (stamped 07:45) | GBP 1.3253 +0.17 | Gold 4,185.26 -0.20 | EURGBP 0.8454 -0.12
   | Gilt 5.42 0.00 (stamped 06:55) | BTC 84,123 +2.19

*** THE GILT BASIS PROBLEM IS RESOLVED — SEVENTH DAY, AND THIS ONE SETTLES IT ***
For six consecutive days CNBC's previous_day_closing for UK10Y-GB has been unusable and the gilt change has
been carried on a declared basis. Today two independent sources agree and they agree on the thing that was
in dispute:
  CNBC live:            5.4197
  Trading Economics:    5.42, daily change -0.004, dated Oct/12
  -> -0.004 implies a Friday close of about 5.4237.
  CNBC's post-cash-close Friday read, recorded in Friday evening's summary: 5.4226.
Those two agree to within 1bp. Friday's TRUE close was therefore ~5.422-5.424, and the 5.4396 we read at
18:15 on Friday — and published as 5.44 — was a stale post-cash-close quote, not a close. The cash gilt
market shuts at 17:00; an 18:15 read is not a close and must stop being treated as one.
  5.4197 - 5.4226 = -0.0029 -> 0.00
So the gilt is published FLAT at 5.42. A reader comparing with Sunday evening's ticker will see 5.44 -> 5.42
and a stated change of 0.00, and the honest explanation is that the 5.44 was 2bp too high, not that the gilt
moved. Published editions are immutable so Friday's and the weekend's figures stand as printed.
LESSON FOR EVERY FUTURE EVENING READ: take the gilt from the post-17:00 CNBC value and corroborate with the
Trading Economics daily change. Do not use an 18:00-18:15 quote as the close.
TE also gives UK 1M 3.85 and UK 3M 4.11, both dated Oct/09.

*** THE REAL STORY IN THIS TICKER: THE GULF PREMIUM DID NOT ARRIVE ***
Brent settled on Friday at 104.72 before a weekend in which Riyadh airport was struck again with fatalities,
a US jet disabled a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman, roughly 69% of US Gulf of Mexico output stayed shut
after Hurricane Isaias, Washington suspended sanctions on Russian diesel, and the US president claimed an
energy ceasefire that Kyiv says has already been broken. Friday evening's summary said Monday's open would
be "the first genuine read" on all of it. The answer is that Brent is DOWN, if only marginally, at 104.60.
Gold is down 0.20 and sterling is up 0.17. That is not a market pricing escalation; it is a market setting
the Russian diesel supply against the Gulf risk and finding them close to cancelling out.
BRENT CROSS-CHECK: Trading Economics 104.50 -0.21% against CNBC 104.60 -0.11%. Agreement on level to 0.10
and on direction; the 0.10 percentage-point gap in the change is within the usual two-provider spread.
WTI on TE: 91.33 -0.57%.
UST CROSS-CHECK: Trading Economics US 10Y 5.24, dated Oct/09, against CNBC 5.242 prev 5.233. Agreement.
US30Y 5.60 (-0.007).

BITCOIN BASIS: 84,123 against Friday's close of 82,322.43 = +2.19. Sunday evening published +1.60 and
Sunday morning +0.89 on that same Friday-close basis, so the series is continuous and bitcoin has added
roughly 1,800 since Friday across a weekend of Gulf escalation.

*** THIRD READ, 08:12 BST — TWO INSTRUMENTS REPRICED AND THE FTSE LAG CONFIRMED AGAIN ***
.FTSE still returned 10,552.05 stamped 2026-10-09 at 08:12, twelve minutes after the London open. That is
the sixth consecutive weekday morning the feed has served the previous close inside the first half-hour,
and it confirms the diagnosis rather than adding to it. The published FTSE therefore stays on Friday's
close with Friday's move, declared.
Two live instruments had moved enough since 07:55 to be worth republishing:
  Brent  104.60 (-0.11) at 07:45  ->  103.93 (-0.75) at 08:02. A 0.6% move in under twenty minutes.
  Gilt   5.4197 (0.00)  at 06:55  ->  5.4119 (-0.01) at 07:12 GMT.
Both are published on the later read. The Brent move strengthens rather than weakens this morning's
reading: crude is now down three quarters of a per cent on the first session after a weekend of Gulf
escalation, which is the opposite of a risk premium and is the point the ticker drivers make.
GILT on the resolved basis: 5.4119 - 5.4226 (Friday's true close) = -0.0107 -> -0.01. Published 5.41 -0.01.
